◆ convert_rcpi_from_rssi()

uint8_t wireless_utils::convert_rcpi_from_rssi ( int8_t  rssi)
static

Makes conversion from RSSI to RCPI.

RCPI means Received channel power indicator. RSSI means Received signal strength indicator.

This method can only return between 0-220 values.

Between 221-254 values are reserved (MultiAP Spec.). 255 means measurement is not avaliable.

Parameters
rssisignal strength mostly negative value.
Returns
converted rcpi value.
Here is the caller graph for this function:

Makes conversion from RCPI to RSSI.

RCPI means Received channel power indicator. RSSI means Received signal strength indicator.

rcpisignal power indicator value.

◆ initialize_channels_table_6g()

const std::map< uint8_t, std::map< beerocks::eWiFiBandwidth, wireless_utils::sChannel > > wireless_utils::initialize_channels_table_6g ( )
staticprivate

Initialized 6GHz channels table variable on son_wireless-utils.cpp.

Instead of initializing a huge map of 6GHz channels, like in channels_table_5g, which will inflate the size of the file in son_wireless_utils.cpp, this function does the same. It is called and assigned once to channels_table_6g member.

Returns
const std::map<uint8_t, std::map<beerocks::eWiFiBandwidth, sChannel>>

same pattern as the global variable variable channels_table_5g. The is the first 160MHz chunk of 6G band. This is used as the pattern to create a full 6GHz channels table. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_WLAN_channels#6_GHz_(802.11ax)

This is used to add 320MHz-1 and 320MHz-2 channels to the 6GHz channels table. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_WLAN_channels#6_GHz_(802.11ax_and_802.11be)

6GHz channels have 7 chunks of 160MHz. Each chunk has 8 channels of 20MHz. For example, the first chunk contains channels between 1 to 29. The second chunk contains channel between 33 to 61. and so on. Each chunk has 1 channel of 320MHz except the last chunk.

  • 320MHz-1(center channels): 31, 95, 159
  • 320MHz-2(center channels): 63, 127, 191 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_WLAN_channels#6_GHz_(802.11ax)
